title: Introduce per-tenant ingest rate governor and multi-tier retention coordinator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Our current audit ingest path allows bursty tenants to create high write amplification in the indexing layer and push large volumes to hot shards, increasing token costs and causing query latency regressions for SSO/SAML admin events and RBAC v2 change logs. Goal: Implement a tenant-aware ingest admission controller (rate governor) with deferred-eviction buffers and a multi-tier retention coordinator that enforces per-tenant TTL, index partitioning, and automatic coldspill policies. This ticket covers design, implementation, load testing, and rollout plan for a conservative P0 ship that prevents single-tenant cost explosions while preserving strict audit fidelity for admin/SAML events.
updates: 2025-01-16 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to admission controller + retention coordinator; decided to keep canonicalization of SSO/SAML admin events in a separate follow-up (to avoid scope creep).

2025-01-20 - Design review: chose token-bucket per-tenant limiter with burst allowance and a soft-queue (deferred-eviction) backed by compact append-only blobs. Trade-off: small additional tail latency vs. large reduction in hot-shard write amplification.

2025-01-24 - Implementation: admission controller prototype implemented in chronicle-proxy. Initial metrics: per-tenant throttling reduced peak writes by ~52% on internal replay with 10x burst traces. Code (internal): GH PR #4823. Requesting review from @michael-cho and @leena-oz.

2025-02-02 - Retention coordinator: introduced multi-tier retention config (hot: 7d, warm: 30d, cold: 365d) with tenant overrides and cost-based hedge. Draft policy stored in Confluence: /confluence/redwood/audit/retention-multitier-2025.
2025-02-05 - Security review: flagged requirement to record RBAC v2 grant/revoke events with immutable sequence IDs and HMAC checksum for tamper evidence. Security review requested (SR-2025-19).

2025-02-07 - Load testing: ran synthetic tenant mix (100 tenants, 1% heavy) on staging; tail P95 ingestion latency increased by 18ms but overall egress cost projection decreased 31% in the cost simulator. Dashboard: /dashboards/audit/ingest-governor-2025.

2025-02-09 - UX/ops: added admin controls to console for emergency override and per-tenant emergency tokens. Discussed RBAC v2 scope: only admins with 'audit:ingest:override' may toggle. Adding audit entries for override actions.
2025-02-10 - Next: finish end-to-end retries for deferred-eviction blobs, finalize canary plan (10% tenants week 1), and open migration playbook for Dedicated customers to adopt per-tenant settings.
notes_for_qa: QA should validate: 1) per-tenant token-bucket enforcement across burst replay, 2) deferred-eviction blob durability under node restarts, 3) retention TTL transitions (hot->warm->cold) and coldspill correctness, and 4) correct immutable audit entries for RBAC v2 grant/revoke and SSO/SAML admin flows.
rollout_plan: Canary 10% tenants (week 1) -> 50% tenants (week 2) -> 100% with automatic rollback on cost anomaly or >1% increase in missed admin events. Ops playbook stored in Confluence.
postmortem_considerations: If we observe missed admin events during rollout, capture full staging replay, preserve deferred blobs for forensic reconstitution, and prioritize reindexing with strong ordering guarantees. Prepare communication template for customers affected by temporary delays in audit visibility.
